pipeline: AI-Driven Computational Pipeline for Ayurvedic Drug Discovery
hard_constraint: Every output maps to 1 of 5 evidentiary tiers. MUST NOT present computational prediction as clinical proof. AYUSH-64 case study justification.

evidence_tiers_definition.1: database-derived information - IMPPAT, PubChem, RCSB PDB curation
evidence_tiers_definition.2: molecular-docking result - AutoDock Vina style score, pose, PLIP interactions
evidence_tiers_definition.3: machine-learning prediction - supervised affinity prediction pKd
evidence_tiers_definition.4: explainable-AI interpretation - SHAP values explaining model attention
evidence_tiers_definition.5: literature-derived / LLM-synthesised evidence - RAG retrieval with citations

target.relevance: AYUSH-64 repurposing case study [3] - computational prediction to RCT, central to evidentiary tier requirement

tier_2_docking_result.disclaimer: DISCLAIMER: Computational docking estimate. Requires experimental validation (SPR, ITC). NOT clinical proof of efficacy per AYUSH-64 guideline. Score is scoring-function estimate not measured Kd.

tier_3_ml_prediction.disclaimer: ML-predicted affinity is statistical inference from synthetic training data. Applicability domain limited. Requires wet-lab validation. NOT clinical proof. Example: predicted pKd 6.8 does NOT mean therapeutic effect.
tier_3_ml_prediction.confidence: Model-dependent; check applicability domain and training distribution

data.query: Gallic acid Triphala anti-inflammatory mechanism AYUSH-64 COVID-19 Mpro repurposing

retrieved_passages.text: Mapping 174 bioactives across Triphala's three herbs onto 44 shared targets and 78 diseases revealed substantially denser bioactive-target pattern for combined formulation than single herbs, supporting synergistic claim. Hub bioactives: gallic acid, ellagic acid, chebulagic acid interacting with COX-2 TNF-alpha.
63 anti-epileptic Ayurvedic herbs screened 349 drug-like phytochemicals against mGluR targets using DrugBank similarity validation heuristic, 11 novel neuromodulator candidates.

AYUSH-64 polyherbal formulation repurposed against COVID-19 using combined network pharmacology and molecular docking and subsequently evaluated in open-label RCT as adjunct. Rare documented example computational hypothesis carried to clinical tier.

data.synthesized_summary: Literature-derived evidence: Gallic acid is reported as hub bioactive in Triphala network pharmacology analysis (174 bioactives, 44 targets, 78 diseases) [4] interacting with COX-2 (PDB 5KIR) and TNF-alpha (2AZ5) inflammatory targets - database-derived association not experimental affinity. AYUSH-64 case study [3] demonstrates computational NP+docking repurposing against COVID-19 Mpro target (PDB 6LU7) progressed to open-label RCT as separate subsequent step - this progression is cautionary template for evidentiary tier separation. Current docking -7.45 kcal/mol for gallic acid vs Mpro is computational hypothesis (Tier 2) and ML predicted pKd 6.82 (Tier 3) is statistical inference; both require wet-lab validation before any clinical claim. RAG performance targets per [28]: hallucination 47.8%->12.3% reduction, faithfulness 0.52->0.87, accuracy 0.54->0.89 when grounded, vs 0% hallucinated citations for RAG vs 40-60% non-RAG [27]. No supporting evidence found for direct clinical efficacy of gallic acid against COVID-19 in retrieved corpus - explicit null state surfaced rather than generating unsupported claim.
data.null_state_example: No clinical trial evidence for gallic acid vs COVID-19 in retrieved corpus - system surfaces 'no supporting evidence found' rather than hallucinating efficacy

ayush64_case_study_justification.lesson: AYUSH-64 repurposing COVID-19 via NP+docking [3] subsequently evaluated in open-label RCT as adjunct - rare documented computational -> clinical tier progression
ayush64_case_study_justification.implication: Underscores why every output must be explicitly labeled by tier rather than undifferentiated result; computational prediction presented as hypothesis not therapy
ayush64_case_study_justification.hard_constraint_enforcement: central module backend/app/core/evidence/tiers.py decorator @enforce_tier and validate_no_clinical_claim blocks phrases claiming clinical proof
